more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Potassium iodate is an inorganic potassium salt of iodic acid. FDA describes manufacture by reacting iodine with potassium hydroxide. The direct-food application in this regulation is dough strengthening during bread manufacture. That application has a flour-based use limit and should be distinguished from separate nutrient or salt-iodisation applications.
more_info.origin: FDA describes chemical preparation by reacting iodine with potassium hydroxide. The resulting potassium iodate is an inorganic salt. The reviewed food-use definition describes synthetic preparation rather than biological extraction.
more_info.uses: Used as a dough strengthener in bread manufacture. The US regulation sets a maximum of 0.0075% relative to flour weight. The bread standard also sets a combined limit for its specified dough-conditioning group.
